channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Defiant Hegseth blasts impeachment effort as 'spectacle,' puts 'target' on troops
item.description: Republican Rep. Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Hegseth on the House floor Monday afternoon.

item.title: Supreme Court lifts pause on border construction in Big Bend, Texas
item.description: The construction will include physical walls, access roads and vehicle barriers, according to Trump administration plans.

item.title: Gas prices dip below $4 but inflation remains stubbornly high
item.description: Gasoline prices fell below $4 a gallon Tuesday for the first time in three months — but the overall cost of living remains stubbornly high. (Image credit: Ronaldo Schemidt)

item.title: 'Like gods reigning over humans': Many defectors see daughter of North Korea's Kim as heir apparent
item.description: Little is known about her except that she's reportedly about 13 and named Kim Ju Ae, but Korea's spy agency says she's likely her father's heir. (Image credit: 朝鮮通信社)

item.title: Indonesia's VP offers resignation as questions mount over his eligibility
item.description: His resignation offer comes amid a widening political rift between Prabowo and Widodo and a separate investigation into allegations that senior police officials wiretapped the president. (Image credit: Dita Alangkara)

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth calls move to impeach him 'sabotage'
item.description: US ​Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday called ​moves to impeach him over abuse of power in the Iran war a farce that ​would ‌fail. The Pentagon chief slammed the move as a "political spectacle" by an outgoing congressional opponent of President Donald Trump.

item.title: The average cost for a new vehicle in the U.S. hits a record high: over $51,000
item.description: Vehicle transaction prices are up to a new record high, according to the Kelley Blue Book — and some buyers are extending their car loans to finance them. (Image credit: Brandon Bell)

item.title: US-mediated talks on ending Russia-Ukraine war begin in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US opened Tuesday, November 10, in the United Arab Emirates, as Washington made another push to end the war. The two-day session in Abu Dhabi is the first such meeting since February. It will focus on establishing future security guarantees for the warring countries.

item.title: French students block dozens of schools, vow more protests
item.description: French students blocked the entrances to dozens of high schools on Tuesday, November 10, as they kept up protests for better learning conditions. These protests across France have spiraled into larger cost-of-living demonstrations in recent weeks, some marked by violence and police brutality. FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago reports from the ground.

item.title: Anthropic values itself at nearly $1.3 trillion, according to new IPO filing
item.description: The company is valuing itself at about $1.3 trillion.

item.title: Seven days of chaos in the ER: How this country's healthcare system is unraveling
item.description: Renewed fighting has pushed Ethiopia's healthcare system close to collapse: "The whole emergency (room) was flooded with war trauma patients," one surgeon says of a brutal week in September. (Image credit: AFP)

item.title: Anthropic seeks $1.4trn valuation amid worry over AI investment
item.description: AI chatbot maker Anthropic is seeking a stock market valuation of up to $1.4trn (£1trn).

item.title: Trump says he'd 'stand by' Hegseth even if he's impeached
item.description: Hegseth said he's "not worried" about an impeachment effort.

item.title: Get in, loser: Broadway's newest 'Mean Girls' are ready to insult (and enlighten) you
item.description: School Girls; Or the African Mean Girls Play during opening night curtain call for the play's Broadway run this fall. In this final week of performances, livestreaming is available. Left to right: Nia Otchere-Sarfo, Jordan Rice, Lucia Aremu, Denee Benton, Heather Alicia Simms, Erin Morton, Jasmine Amy Rogers and Patina Miller.'/> "School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play," is ending a Broadway run this week and celebrating with livestream broadcasts. We interviewed the Tony-nominated playwright, Jocelyn Bioh. (Image credit: Bruce Glikas)

item.title: WATCH: Officer shot 6 times celebrates wedding
item.description: Five months after Buffalo Police Officer Marc Hurst was shot six times while on duty, he celebrated a moment that once seemed far from certain: marrying his fiancee, Haley.

item.title: Poundland owner releases £10m to retailer hours before MP grilling
item.description: Poundland's owner has released millions of pounds of funding to pay the discount retailer's suppliers - a breakthrough in talks about saving the discount retailer and its 10,500 staff.

item.title: Ukraine peace talks: Who is sitting at the negotiating table – and why it matters
item.description: Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened Tuesday in the United Arab Emirates, as Washington made a renewed push to end the war that followed Moscow's invasion of its neighbour nearly five years ago. As these two days of talks in Abu Dhabi get underway, the negotiators that each country has chosen to send tell us most of what we need to know about what will be discussed, as FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert explains.

item.title: Scots urged to use A&E 'only when necessary' amid 'significant pressures'
item.description: Scotland's A&E departments are under "significant pressures" heading into winter, the nation's health secretary has conceded.

item.title: Dana White: UFC chief declines Trump’s White House job offer
item.description: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White made a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday to turn down Donald Trump’s offer of a job as the White House press secretary, saying he has “zero political aspirations”. Trump stunned the world on November 7 when he said on social media that he had offered White the job, only to claim a day later that he was "only kidding”.

item.title: WATCH: Woman living the 'dream' to save foxes in need
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a woman who's on a mission to save foxes at a sanctuary in upstate New York.

item.title: Sen. Duckworth wants VA to identify toxic threats before veterans get sick
item.description: Sen. Tammy Duckworth to introduce legislation that would require VA to more quickly assess toxic hazards, expanding access to health care and disability benefits.

item.title: Why did California's billionaire tax fail to surf the blue wave?
item.description: Two economists debate what California's vote on Prop 40 means for the wealth tax movement. (Image credit: FREDERIC J. BROWN/AFP via Getty Images)

item.title: New Israel parliament to be sworn in as Eisenkot works to form new govt
item.description: Israel's new parliament will be sworn on Tuesday, November 10, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu set to lose his majority as rival Gadi Eisenkot works to form a new government. The opposition hopes to use its newfound legislative power to move quickly on key priorities, including a commission to investigate security failures under Netanyahu that allowed the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Jerusalem Noga Tarnopolsky has more.

item.title: California voters reject measure to tax the wealth of billionaires
item.description: California voters have rejected a first-in-the-nation tax on the net worth of billionaires following a contentious ballot fight that generated huge spending by some prominent tech leaders eager to stop their taxes from going up. The measure would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Los Angeles Loic Pialat has more.

item.title: Teddy Riner: From French Olympic judo champion to presidential candidate
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Tuesday, November 10: French Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announces he will run for president in next year's French elections. But how serious is his bid? Also, a new government directive in France says schoolchildren must participate in Remembrance Day commemorations – but the unions are not happy. British comedian Russell Brand is sentenced to 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault. Finally, we bring you the best of the memes on Nvidia's Jensen Huang.

item.title: US Hegseth faces Republican impeachment bid over abuse of power in Iran war
item.description: A Republican lawmaker moved on Monday to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war in Iran, setting the stage for a potentially explosive vote in Congress, days after President Donald Trump's party suffered a crushing defeat in the midterms. Kentucky Congressman Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment, accusing Hegseth of waging war illegally without congressional authorisation and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief.

item.title: China's charm offensive pays off as foreign tourism rebounds
item.description: How is tourism faring in China seven years after the Covid-19 pandemic? The country reopened its borders in 2023 and is playing the charm card to restore its image. A strategy that’s paying off: last year the number of tourists exceeded pre-pandemic levels, and French travelers are among those flocking there.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine hold nearly 4 hours of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Hopes of progress in ending Europe's biggest conflict since World War II are tempered by the absence of any significant breakthroughs in three previous rounds of talks early this year. (Image credit: Altaf Qadri)

item.title: Paraguayan protesters are back on the streets despite the removal of President
item.description: A banking crisis that saw the president of Paraguay impeached Friday, November 6, continues to rock the country with protesters back on the streets. The Ueno Bank started as a digital first bank, attracting many low income customers, quickly growing to become a major bank in charge of state pensions and holding the accounts of several government institutions before having its accounts frozen by the central bank due to solvency concerns.

item.title: France vows tough response to freezer cyberattack blamed on Iran
item.description: France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Tuesday, November 10, that Paris ruled out "nothing" to respond to a major cyberattack on hundreds of supermarket fridges in October that it has blamed on Iran. The goal, Jean-Noel Barrot told France Info, is "to deter anyone who might be tempted, in Iran or elsewhere, to do it again".

item.title: Seniors rock the stage: Greek theater seeks to show that 'art has no age'
item.description: A recent Greek National Opera production afforded a group of seniors the chance to channel their young-at-heart energy into onstage performances, proving that no one's too old to learn something new. It challenged the premise that retirement means surrendering to a sedentary lifestyle and extinguishing one’s creative spirit.

item.title: Peru gets ready to welcome Pope Leo XIV on his South America tour
item.description: Pope Leo XIV continued his South American tour on Wednesday, November 11, with a visit to Peru, after stops in Uruguay and Argentina. The American-born pontiff lived in Peru for several years and even became a Peruvian citizen. Ahead of his arrival, the country unveiled a giant statue in his honour.

item.title: US Republican Thomas Massie launches bid to impeach Pete Hegseth
item.description: US Republican Thomas Massie moved Monday, November 9, to force a vote to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, pressing his fellow Republicans to remove one of the Trump administration's most prominent figures following sweeping election losses blamed in part on fallout from the war in Iran. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Washington Fraser Jackson has more.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine hold US-backed talks after Trump says broad deal is possible
item.description: Russian and Ukrainian officials met on Tuesday, November 10, for their first US-brokered talks since February, after US President Donald Trump suggested last week that a broad deal was possible on ending the war in Ukraine and guaranteeing security in Europe. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Kyiv Emmanuelle Chaze and FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson have more.

item.title: At least 12 killed in Bulgaria motorway pile-ups involving dozens of vehicles
item.description: At least 12 people have been killed in two motorway pile-ups in eastern Bulgaria, the country's health minister said.

item.title: Pupils at Edinburgh Academy suffered decades of 'dreadful abuse'
item.description: Pupils at Edinburgh Academy suffered "dreadful abuse" over four decades while the school sought to protect its reputation and ignored complaints, the Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry has found.

item.title: China's 'impossible to ignore' tech rise on display at Web Summit in Lisbon
item.description: One of Europe's biggest annual tech events, the Web Summit, kicked off in the Portuguese capital this week with the biggest ever delegation of Chinese business leaders and policymakers. FRANCE 24's Charles Pellegrin talks to Dr. Dan Wang, China Director at Eurasia Group, about EU-China tech relations, the climate of suspicion created by the spying scandal at Nvidia, and what the EU's quest for tech sovereignty could mean for China.

item.title: Inspiring Senegal's next generation: Free tickets bring children to Dakar 2026
item.description: As part of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, 200,000 free tickets will be distributed to schools and community organisations. The aim is to give as many young people as possible the chance to experience the Games. FRANCE 24’s team on the ground reports.

item.title: South Africa's ANC slumps to worst-ever election result
item.description: The African National Congress, which has dominated South African politics since the end of apartheid, took 30.76 percent of votes in municipal elections, its worst-ever electoral performance, the electoral commission said Sunday. With no party winning outright in many municipalities, the results set the stage for fraught multiparty coalition negotiations to govern several major cities.

item.title: Ugandan former intelligence officer exposes alleged army abuses
item.description: In Uganda, a former military intelligence officer accused the army of secretly detaining and torturing opponents in clandestine houses. In late September, Lieutenant Herbert Matanda Mabonga released videos that sparked an outcry in the country and were widely shared on social media. FRANCE 24 correspondent in the region spoke with him from his place of exile.

item.title: House Republicans to elect a new leader as they look to rebuild from midterm defeat
item.description: After sweeping losses in the midterm elections, the House GOP will vote on Tuesday to elect a successor to Mike Johnson, who says he's stepping down as the chamber's top Republican. (Image credit: J. Scott Applewhite)

item.title: Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as Eisenkot prepares government
item.description: Israel's new parliament is set to be sworn in Tuesday with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot's camp holding a majority. Eisenkot seeks to build a coalition after receiving a mandate to form a government.

item.title: Fossil fuel emissions set to fall for first time since Covid, research shows
item.description: Global fossil fuel emissions are expected to fall by 0.4 percent in 2026 for first time since the Covid pandemic, driven by the expansion of renewable energy and the oil price shock linked to the Iran war, researchers said Tuesday, who warned the decline may be short-lived.

item.title: France threatens actions against Iran over supermarket cyberattacks
item.description: France will seek European-level sanctions against Iran in response to cyberattacks on hundreds of supermarket fridges, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Tuesday, after accusing Tehran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating the October sabotage.

item.title: Teddy Riner announces candidacy for French presidential elections
item.description: French Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential elections, against a backdrop of political tension across France.

item.title: Storms hitting UK at same time led to one of country's wettest days on record
item.description: Storms Austen and Boelo striking different parts of the UK at the same time contributed to 24 October being one of the wettest days Britain has ever seen.

item.title: FBI investigating Nvidia CEO over affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: Donald Trump has said the FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy - but insisted he is a "very honourable man".

item.title: WATCH: 'Love is Blind' season 11, Erika Kirk: Here's what's trending
item.description: ABC's Rocsi Diaz takes a look at what's buzzing, including the Netflix series reunion not holding back and Erika Kirk speaking out after Dave Chappelle joked about her husband's assassination.

item.title: WATCH: What to expect from Bills-Vikings showdown
item.description: ESPN's Cameron Wolfe helps preview the matchup.

item.title: WATCH: Inside the shadowy world of counterespionage
item.description: International Spy Museum's executive director Col. Chris Costa discusses the possible tactics the suspected Chinese spy used in the Nvidia scandal.

item.title: WATCH: Vikings' Aaron Jones shaped by military service
item.description: ABC News' Rebecca Jarvis reports ahead of the Vikings' Salute to Service game as running back Aaron Jones earns a nomination for the NFL's Salute to Service Award.

item.title: WATCH: New reaction to White House shake-up as newly elected Democrats head to Washington
item.description: President Donald Trump blamed bad messaging for the GOP's losses amid a White House shake-up that saw Stephen Miller, the architect of Trump's hard-line immigration policy, promoted to chief of staff.

item.title: WATCH: Disney launches 'Make the Holidays Magic' campaign
item.description: Disney kicks off the holiday season with a new short film called, “A Disney Holiday Short: The Invisible Horse.”

item.title: DOJ leadership shakeup continues as Civil Division chief steps down
item.description: The head of the Justice Department's Civil Division, Brett Shumate, has submitted his resignation, becoming the latest DOJ leader to step down following the midterms.

item.title: France blames Iran for massive cyber attack on supermarket fridges
item.description: France has accused Iran of being behind the massive cyber attack on supermarket fridges last month.

item.title: Jan. 6 should follow Trump 'to his grave,' Biden says in new memoir
item.description: Biden also said Trump "bordered on fawning" during 2024 Oval Office meeting

item.title: WATCH: Vikings superfan has only missed 2 home games in 25 seasons
item.description: “GMA” is outside U.S. Bank Stadium with Minnesota Vikings “Fan of the Year,” Lindsey Lorenston, as she is surprised with a pair of tickets to Super Bowl LXI.

item.title: Trump says he plans 'tremendous numbers' of pardons in 2nd half of term
item.description: The president also defended his pardons of Jan. 6 rioters.

item.title: WATCH: Trump now showing 'great level of political acumen,' former staffer says
item.description: Harrison Fields served as the White House principal deputy press secretary from January to August 2025.

item.title: WATCH: Pope Leo XIV in Argentina
item.description: The pontiff will celebrate his first mass in Buenos Aires on Monday, which is expected to draw more than a million people.

item.title: WATCH: Family's gigantic fern named 'Jeff' goes viral on social media
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a family in Colorado who has an annual tradition of having to move their gigantic fern, named Jeff, back inside for autumn.

item.title: Explosion at steel plant in Turkey kills 16, president says
item.description: A major fire broke out following an explosion at an iron and steel plant in Turkey on Monday killing 16 people, the country's president confirmed.

item.title: Trump says 'too tough' deportation policies hurt him in the midterms
item.description: "I think it was too tough," Trump said in an interview with CBS' "60 Minutes" that aired Sunday night. "And I think -- I think ultimately, that hurt me," he added.

item.title: At least 14 dead after boat carrying migrants found near Crete
item.description: At least 14 people have died after a boat carrying migrants was found near Crete, Greek authorities have said.

item.title: WATCH: NASA recruiting next generation of astronauts
item.description: NASA has released a new recruitment video, looking for new space explorers as it works to create a permanent base on the moon and someday possibly launching humans to Mars.

item.title: Finland's navy chief says Russia's presence in the Baltic Sea may have peaked for now
item.description: Russia may have reached the limit of its "peacetime" ability to project force in the Baltic Sea, with the maritime situation "tense" but "stable", the head of Finland's navy has said.

item.title: WATCH: Firefighters give kids a superhero surprise
item.description: Corpus Christi firefighters dressed as superheroes surprised patients at Driscoll Children's Hospital by rappelling down the glass building as kids waved.

item.title: Democrats flip statehouses in midterm wave
item.description: The showing across the country that flipped Congress to Democratic control on Election Day also trickled down to the state and local level.

item.title: Gunman suspected of killing six people in Polish city of Krakow has died, police say
item.description: A gunman suspected of killing six people including a British national in Poland on Saturday has died in hospital.
